complexity.correctness_note: Unreachable through NeetCode's own judge, which drops empty lists while deserializing: Example 3 arrives as [] rather than [None], so the submission passes. That serializer bug is reported at https://github.com/neetcode-gh/leetcode/issues/5798 . Probed directly — a solution returning len(lists) answers 0 for lists=[[]].
complexity.correctness_reason: Crashes with AttributeError on any input containing an empty list among the k — e.g. lists = [[1,2],[],[3]] — because vals = [node.val for node in lists] dereferences the None head, and the main loop reads lists[j].val on it too. The constraints permit this (0 <= lists[i].length <= 500), and Example 3 is lists = [[]].
complexity.notes: The vals list is built and maintained but never read, making it dead code (and it is what crashes on empty lists). The tie-break on prev.val is an unnecessary micro-optimization. A heap or divide-and-conquer merge would give O(n log k).
complexity.summary: Selection-merge: for each output node, it linearly scans all k list heads to find the smallest value (with a shortcut that grabs the first head equal to the previously appended value), appends it, and advances that list. With total nodes n and up to k = n lists, this is O(n*k) = O(n^2).
